subject: Art & Design
title: Streaming Wars: How Distribution Changed Cinema
description: One-minute skill: Streaming Wars: How Distribution Changed Cinema.

hook.text: Netflix spent $17 billion on content in a single year. More than most countries' entire film industries combined.

buildup.text: Streaming platforms disrupted the theatrical release model. Films now premiere on screens in your pocket.

discovery.text: The window between theater and home release shrank from months to days. Some films skip theaters entirely.

twist.text: Scorsese called Marvel films 'not cinema.' The debate about what counts as cinema intensified.

climax.text: International films found global audiences through streaming. Parasite's Oscar win was partly a streaming effect.

punchline.text: Cinema isn't dying. It's moving to a different screen.

quiz.question: How has streaming changed international cinema?
options: International films found global audiences they couldn't reach through theaters alone
Only Hollywood films are available on streaming

details.summary: Netflix, Amazon, Disney+, and other streaming platforms transformed cinema by making films available instantly worldwide, bypassing theatrical release. The streaming model favors quantity, algorithmic recommendation, and home viewing.
details.whyItMatters: Streaming's disruption of theatrical distribution is cinema's biggest existential challenge since the arrival of television. How the industry resolves the tension between accessibility and theatrical experience will define cinema's future.
takeaways: Streaming platforms bypass traditional theatrical distribution
The model favors quantity and algorithmic recommendation
The theater vs. streaming tension defines cinema's future

faq.question: Are streaming-produced films real cinema?
faq.answer: This debate rages in the industry. Martin Scorsese and Christopher Nolan argue cinema requires theatrical viewing. Others note Netflix funds ambitious films no studio would greenlight. Technically, a film is a film regardless of distribution.

faq.question: Will movie theaters survive streaming?
faq.answer: Likely yes, but in reduced numbers and transformed form. Theaters are becoming premium experiences with better screens, sound, and seating. Event films (blockbusters, horror) that benefit from communal viewing will sustain theaters. Mid-budget dramas have largely migrated to streaming permanently.
